Architecture.description:
A complete NNUE architecture: input features, feature transformer
(accumulator), dense layers, output buckets and quantization.

$schema.description: Optional link to this schema, for editors. Ignored.

accumulator.description: Feature transformer: the first, sparse layer, updated incrementally.

hiddenLayers.description:
Dense layers between the accumulator and the output, in order. The
output layer (one neuron, no activation) is implicit.

metadata.description: Descriptive information. Not part of the architecture hash.

outputBuckets.description:
Several sets of weights for the layers after the accumulator, one of
which is chosen by the position.

quantization.description: How weights and activations are stored as integers.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the architecture schema. Always 1.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page; absent on the last one.

BucketScope.description:
Layers with one set of weights per bucket.
- `output`: The output layer only.
- `all`: Every layer after the accumulator ("layer stacks").

BucketStrategy.description:
Bucket selection.
- `none`: A single set of weights.
- `pieceCount`: `(pieces − 2) / (32 / count)`, pieces counted with the kings.
- `material`: `min(count − 1, material · count / 79)`, material counted P=1, N=B=3, R=5, Q=9 for both sides (78 at the start).

Elo relative to the first player, fitted over the games of every

Nodes per second measured by its latest evaluation (on that
evaluation's worker: compare speeds measured on the same machine).

players.description: The players, in the order asked.

scores.description:
Search scores (White's point of view), bins of 100 centipawns from

DenseShape.description: A dense layer as stored: `buckets` sets of `outputs × inputs` weights.

activation.description: Activation after the layer; `None` for the output layer.

sum.description: Integer type of the dot products.

accumulatorBytes.description: Memory of one accumulator (both perspectives), copied at every ply.

kingRefreshes.description: Whether king moves can force refreshes.

i16 additions to rebuild one perspective from scratch (king bucket

weightsBytes.description:
Size of the quantized weights, in bytes (the network file adds a

EvaluationJob.description:
An evaluation match, fully resolved: the candidate plays pairs of games
against the baseline from the same random opening with colors swapped.

baseline.description: The engine it is measured against.

games.description: Games to play at most (an even number).

moveTimeMs.description: Milliseconds per move, instead of nodes.

oneOf.description: Stops as soon as this test concludes; without it, every game is played.

EvaluationProgress.description: Latest result of an evaluation match, from the candidate's side.

baselineNps.description: Nodes per second of the baseline's search, on the same worker.

candidateNps.description:
Nodes per second of the candidate's search (one thread, measured
by the worker before the match).

elo.description: Elo difference of the candidate over the baseline.

eloError.description: Half-width of the 95 % confidence interval of `elo`.

los.description: Likelihood of superiority: probability that the candidate is stronger.

oneOf.description: The SPRT, when the match runs one.

EvaluationRequest.description: An evaluation match, as a client asks for it.

oneOf.description: The model it plays against (default: the classical evaluation).

games.description: Games to play at most, 2 to 100000 (rounded up to pairs).

moveTimeMs.description:
Milliseconds per move, 10 to 60000, instead of nodes: a slower
network then searches less. Not reproducible.

nodes.description:
Nodes searched per move, 100 to 10000000 (default 5000 unless
`moveTimeMs` is given). Matches at fixed nodes are reproducible.

seed.description: Seed of the openings (default: drawn at random, then recorded).

oneOf.description: Stop as soon as this test concludes (default: play every game).

x-enum-descriptions: Own/opponent × 5 non-king kinds × 64 squares, per king bucket.

Own/opponent × 5 non-king kinds + kings × 64 squares, per king
bucket, horizontally mirrored.

Features.description:
Input features.

Each perspective sees the board from its own side: squares are flipped
vertically for Black, and pieces are "own" or "opponent". With king
buckets, the features are repeated once per bucket and the bucket of the
perspective's own king selects which copy is active.

kingBuckets.description:
Bucket of each square of the perspective's own king, 64 entries from
a1 (index 0, own back rank) to h8 (index 63). Ids are 0..N-1, all
used. Default: one bucket for `Chess768`, one per square for
`HalfKP`, one per square of files a–d for `HalfKAv2_hm`.

mirror.description:
Horizontal mirroring: with `kingFile`, a perspective whose own king
stands on files e–h sees the board mirrored (a↔h), so its king is
always on files a–d. Default: `kingFile` for `HalfKAv2_hm`, `none`
otherwise.

perspective.description:
Two accumulators, one per side, the side to move's first in the
next layer's input. Without it, a single accumulator sees the board
as White and the result is negated when Black is to move.

FieldError.description: One problem of a request, located by a JSON pointer.

message.description: What is wrong, and usually how to fix it.

path.description: JSON pointer (RFC 6901) to the offending value; `""` is the whole body.

Histogram.description:
Counts of values in bins of equal width, with the values below the
first bin in `below` and those past the last in `above`.

min.description: Lower bound of the first bin (inclusive).

Hyperparameters.description: How a network is trained. Every field has a default.

learningRate.description: AdamW learning rate at the start.

lrDropEvery.description:
The learning rate is multiplied by `lrDropFactor` every
`lrDropEvery` superbatches.

scoreScale.description: Centipawns per unit of the sigmoid of the target and the loss.

shuffleRecords.description: Positions shuffled together by the loader (32 bytes of memory each).

superbatches.description: Superbatches to train (a checkpoint is saved after each).

wdl.description:
Weight of the game result in the target; the rest is the search
score: `(1 − wdl)·σ(score / scoreScale) + wdl·result`.

attempt.description: Times a worker took it (resumes count).

finishedAt.description: When it reached a final status.

oneOf.description: Latest progress reported by its worker.

startedAt.description: When a worker first took it.

worker.description: Worker holding it, or that held it last.

JobEvent.description: Something that happened to a job, in order (`seq` grows across jobs).

seq.description: Position in the log of all events.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page; absent on the last one.

JobSpec.description: What a job does, with all its parameters.

JobStatus.description:
Where a job is in its life.

```text
queued ──claim──▶ running ──▶ succeeded | failed
  │                 │ stop          │ worker lost (no heartbeat)
  ▼                 ▼               ▼
canceled         stopping ──▶ stopped     interrupted
                                 └──── resume ───┴──▶ queued
```

`failed` training jobs can be resumed too (from their last checkpoint).

dense.description: Hidden layers, then the output layer.

ftOutputs.description: Accumulator outputs per perspective after its activation.

ftWeightMax.description: Largest quantized feature transformer weight or bias.

kingRefreshes.description: Whether a king move can force a full refresh of its perspective.

planes.description: Planes of 64 squares per king bucket.

tags.description: Lowercase labels: letters, digits and dashes.

MetricPoint.description: One point of a training curve.

Metrics.description:
The training curve of a run: one point per superbatch (resumed runs
may repeat superbatches trained again after a checkpoint).

Mirror.description:
Horizontal mirroring of the features.
- `none`: Never mirrored.
- `kingFile`: Mirrored when the perspective's own king is on files e–h.

nextCursor.description: Cursor of the next page; absent on the last one.

active.description: Whether it is the active model.

ModelView.description: A model, and whether the engine plays with it.

count.description:
Number of buckets: required unless the strategy is `none`. With
`pieceCount`, a divisor of 32.

scope.description:
Bucketed layers: the output layer only (default) or every layer
after the accumulator.

strategy.description: How a position picks its bucket.

PairResult.description: The games between two players of a comparison.

a.description: Index of the first player in `players`.

b.description: Index of the second player (always greater than `a`).

eloError.description: Half-width of the 95 % confidence interval of `elo`.

Problem.description:
An error (RFC 9457). `type` identifies the kind of problem
(`urn:chess-bot:problem:<name>`); validation problems list every error
found in `errors`.

detail.description: What went wrong with this request.

errors.description: Every problem of the request body, for validation errors.

title.description: Short summary of the kind of problem.

Provenance.description: How a model was made: enough to train it again.

Quantization.description:
Integer storage of the network.

Accumulator values are stored ×`qa` (1.0 ↔ `qa`), dense weights ×`qb`,
dense biases ×`qa·qb` in i32. Every activation brings values back to the
`qa` scale, and the network output is `sum · evalScale / (qa · qb)`
centipawns.

evalScale.description: Centipawns per unit of network output (the trainer's sigmoid scale).

ftWeightClip.description:
Bound on feature transformer weights and biases during training, so
that the i16 accumulator never overflows. Default: the largest safe
value, `⌊32767 / (max active features + 1)⌋ / qa`.

qa.description: Scale of the accumulator: an activation of 1.0 is `qa`.

weightClip.description:
Bound on dense weights during training. Default: the largest value
the weight type holds, `127 / qb` (i8) or `32767 / qb` (i16).

weights.description: Type of the dense layers' weights.

oneOf.description: Network playing the games; `None`: the classical evaluation.

SelfplayProgress.description: Latest progress of a self-play job.

SelfplayRequest.description: A self-play dataset, as a client asks for it.

name.description: Name of the dataset (default: from the parameters).

oneOf.description: Model playing the games (default: the classical evaluation).

seed.description: Seed (default: drawn at random, then recorded).

SelfplayStarted.description: A self-play run and the dataset it fills.

dataset.description: The dataset, `generating` until the run ends.

Sprt.description:
A sequential probability ratio test: is the first player at least
`elo1` stronger (H1), or at most `elo0` (H0)?

alpha.description: Probability of accepting H1 when H0 holds.

beta.description: Probability of accepting H0 when H1 holds.

llr.description: Log-likelihood ratio of H1 against H0.

lowerBound.description: H0 is accepted when the LLR falls to this bound.

upperBound.description: H1 is accepted when the LLR rises to this bound.

SumWidth.description: Integer type in which a dense layer sums its inputs.
x-enum-descriptions: Needed when inputs × activation × weight can exceed 2³⁰.

TrainingJob.description: A training job, fully resolved: everything needed to reproduce it.

seed.description: Seed of the initialization and of the data order.

TrainingProgress.description: Latest progress of a training job.

learningRate.description: Learning rate of the last superbatch.

loss.description: Mean loss of the last superbatch.

vramUsedMb.description: GPU memory in use, when on a GPU.

TrainingRequest.description: A training job, as a client asks for it.

seed.description: Seed (default: drawn at random, then recorded).

ValidationReport.description: Result of a validation: the errors, or what the architecture resolves to.

valid.description: Whether the document is a valid architecture.

WeightType.description:
Dense weights integer type.
- `i8`: 8-bit weights.
- `i16`: 16-bit weights.

info.description:
Declare NNUE architectures, upload or generate datasets, train networks, evaluate them in matches and manage the resulting models.

Authentication: an API key in the `X-API-Key` header. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`); lists page with `limit` and `cursor`; creations accept an `Idempotency-Key` header (kept 24 h). Limits: requests per minute per key (429 with `Retry-After`), size of uploads (413).

Queues an evaluation match: the candidate model plays pairs of games
against the baseline (a model, or the classical evaluation) from the
same random opening with colors swapped, at a fixed number of nodes
(reproducible) or time per move. With `sprt`, the match stops as soon
as the test concludes. The worker first measures the speed (nodes per
second) of both engines.

get.summary:
An evaluation, with its latest result: W/D/L, Elo difference ± its
95 % error, likelihood of superiority, SPRT status, and the speed of
both engines. Its `spec` describes both contestants (name,
architecture, size), even once their models are deleted.

Queues a training run. Everything needed to reproduce it is recorded:
the normalized architecture, the content hash of each dataset, the
hyperparameters and the seed (drawn when not given).

get.summary:
Live events of a training run (Server-Sent Events): `status`,
`progress`, `checkpoint`, `model`, `log`. Each event's `id` is its
sequence number; reconnecting with `Last-Event-ID` (or `after`)
resumes after it. The stream replays the run's history first, and ends
once the run is over.
The training curve: loss, learning rate and speed per superbatch.

post.summary:
Queues a stopped, interrupted or failed training run again: it resumes
from its last checkpoint.

Stops a training run: a queued run is canceled, a running one saves a
checkpoint at the end of its superbatch and stops.
